title: Ted Lasso Returns for Season 4 on Apple TV With Women's Football Focus
excerpt: Jason Sudeikis brings back TV's most beloved coach on August 5, this time leading AFC Richmond's second-division women's team in what co-creator Bill Lawrence says is the start of a new three-season arc.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ted Lasso Season 4 premieres August 5, 2026, with 10 episodes airing weekly.
  • Jason Sudeikis returns to coach AFC Richmond's women's team, continuing the series' legacy.
  • Co-creator Bill Lawrence confirmed a three-season arc for the new storyline.
  • The show will address gender gaps in sports through its narrative and character interactions.
Ted Lasso's Return: Key Details
›Premiere Date: August 5, 2026
›Total Episodes: 10 weekly episodes until October 7
›New Focus: Coaching AFC Richmond's women's team
›Three-Season Arc: Planned by Jason Sudeikis

The Coach Who Was Done — Until He Wasn't

Three years after Jason Sudeikis declared the story of Ted Lasso "done" following a Season 3 finale that sent his character home to Kansas, Apple TV's most decorated comedy is back. Season 4 of Ted Lasso premieres August 5, 2026, with 10 episodes dropping weekly through October 7.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PxZg4SfIURg

The return had been building since March 2025, when Apple formally announced the new season. Production began in July 2025, with Sudeikis, co-creator Bill Lawrence, Brendan Hunt, and Brett Goldstein all returning as executive producers. Goldstein also serves as a writer, and the team added Emmy-winning producer Jack Burditt, whose credits include Modern Family, 30 Rock, and Frasier.

In an interview with Deadline, Lawrence confirmed that Sudeikis has a three-season arc planned for this new chapter — meaning Ted Lasso could run through a potential Season 6 if viewership holds.

A New Team, A New Mission

Season 4 follows Ted as he returns to England to coach AFC Richmond's second-division women's football team. The official logline reads: "Throughout the course of the season, Ted and the team learn to leap before they look, taking chances they never thought they would." Sudeikis told Deadline the characters will discover that "wherever they land, it's exactly where they're meant to be."

The shift to women's football connects to a Season 3 thread where Keeley (Juno Temple) pitched the idea of a women's team to Rebecca (Hannah Waddingham). Trailers hint at the show tackling the gender gap in sports coverage and funding — in one scene, a man welcomes Ted back to England before dismissing him for "coaching a bunch of girls."

"If the Lasso way is wrong, it's hard to imagine being right."

— Trent Crimm, The Richmond Way

The Returning and the New

The core cast is back: Waddingham as Rebecca, Temple as Keeley, Goldstein as Roy Kent, Hunt as Coach Beard, and Jeremy Swift as Leslie Higgins. Grant Feely takes over the role of Ted's now-12-year-old son Henry from Gus Turner, and Andrea Anders is expected to return as Ted's ex-wife Michelle.

Cultural Impact of Ted Lasso
›Debuted in August 2020 during COVID-19 pandemic
›Won 13 Emmy Awards, including Outstanding Comedy Series
›Themes of kindness and self-belief resonate globally
›Significant following among South Asian viewers

Several new actors join the cast, many playing women's football players: Tanya Reynolds (Sex Education), Jude Mack (Back In Action), Faye Marsay (Adolescence), Rex Hayes, Aisling Sharkey, and Abbie Hern. Phil Dunster, who played Jamie Tartt, is not confirmed — he is currently starring in another Bill Lawrence comedy, Rooster. Actor Anthony Head, who played villain Rupert Mannion, passed away in June 2026. It remains unclear how the show will address his character's absence.

![Ted Lasso. Key Takeaways Ted Lasso Season 4 premieres August 5, 2026, with 10 episodes airing weekly.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/7/73/Tedlassotitlecard.jpg)

A World Cup Warm-Up

Sudeikis gave Ted Lasso a global stage on July 19 when he and Hunt appeared in character at the FIFA World Cup Final halftime show in the United States. The pair "substituted" Justin Bieber into the 12-minute performance — which also featured Madonna, BTS, and Shakira — with Hunt holding a substitute board reading "BELIEBE" and Sudeikis telling Bieber, "go out there, don't be nervous, nobody's watching." It marked the first halftime show in World Cup Final history.

Why It Still Resonates

Ted Lasso debuted in August 2020 during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic and became a cultural touchstone, winning 13 Emmy Awards over its original three-season run, including two consecutive trophies for Outstanding Comedy Series. The show's central themes — processing trauma, believing in yourself, the power of kindness in competitive environments — struck a chord with audiences worldwide, including a substantial following among South Asian viewers drawn to its blend of sports, humor, and emotional depth.

What's Ahead

The first episode, titled "Home," was directed by Declan Lowney. If the three-season plan holds, this return represents the start of an entirely new story arc rather than a simple victory lap. The question hanging over Season 4 is whether Ted's signature brand of optimism and empathy can transform a women's team the way it did AFC Richmond's men — and whether the show itself can recapture the magic that made it appointment television during a very different era.

nri_angle: The Emmy-winning comedy has a dedicated following among South Asian viewers globally and returns with themes of equity in sports that parallel growing women's cricket and football discussions in India.
